To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the oil price shock that occurred between 2002-2008 increased the income of cities in the countries considered in this paper that are near a port by 7 percent, and that the effect is stronger for cities connected to the ports by paved roads than for cities connected to ports by unpaved roads.
a 10 percent increase in the cost of transport to the port increases the income of a city near the port by 7 percent, while it increases the income of cities 500 kilometers away by 1.5 percent.
an oil price shock of 2008 magnitude induces the income of sub-Sahara African cities near the port to increase by about 7% relative to cities 500 km further away from the port.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of transport costs in the development of sub-Saharan Africa.
the impact of transport costs on the income of African cities.
the effects of trade on urban growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of transport costs on city incomes depends on the quality of transport infrastructure, the size of the city and the location of the city in relation to the port.
transport costs are an important determinant of city income in Sub-Saharan Africa.
transport costs matter for urban development in sub-Saharan Africa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

transport costs are an important determinant of urban growth in sub- Saharan Africa, and that the impact is heterogeneous depending on the type of roads between cities and their location with respect to the port.

transport costs matter for the economic development of cities in sub-Saharan Africa, and the effect of transport costs on city incomes is larger for cities connected to secondary centers than cities connected to the main port.
the cost of transportation has a strong impact on the economic growth of African cities, especially those that are not well connected to the main port of the country.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transport costs to the nearest port are a key driver of city growth, but that the impact of transport costs on city growth is not uniform.
the urban hierarchy of Africa is shaped by transport costs and that, as a result, the growth prospects of cities depend on the quality of their transport infrastructure.
the impact of transport costs on city income is not only significant but also asymmetric, with cities near the port benefiting more than others.
